questions.question: Height of Tropopause at equator is
questions.explanation: The tropopause is highest at the equator, typically between 16-18 km, due to strong convection.

questions.question: Mother of Pearl clouds occur in
questions.explanation: Mother of Pearl (Nacreous) clouds are rare polar stratospheric clouds found in the stratosphere.

questions.question: Flying from Delhi to Kolkata at constant indicated altitude but experiencing drift to Starboard. The actual altitude will be (vis-à-vis) indicated
questions.explanation: Drift to starboard indicates a crosswind from the left (port side). In the Northern Hemisphere, this suggests the aircraft is in a region where the pressure gradient causes the actual altitude to be higher than indicated when flying from west to east.

questions.question: 850hPa in ISA approximately corresponds to the height
questions.explanation: In the ISA, the 850 hPa pressure level corresponds approximately to 5,000 ft (about 1.5 km).

questions.question: Hot bodies (like sun) radiate
questions.explanation: Hot bodies like the sun radiate primarily in short wavelengths (visible and ultraviolet), while cooler bodies radiate long waves (infrared).

questions.question: Coriolis force is strongest at
questions.explanation: Coriolis force is strongest at the poles and zero at the equator, increasing with latitude.

questions.question: Instrument used for measuring visibility is called
questions.explanation: A transmissometer measures visibility by determining the extinction coefficient of light through the atmosphere.

questions.question: Fog is __
questions.explanation: Fog is essentially a stratus cloud that forms at ground level, reducing visibility to less than 1000m.

questions.question: Showers occur from
questions.explanation: Showers (intermittent, heavy precipitation) occur primarily from cumulonimbus (CB) clouds.

questions.question: Showery precipitation occurs from
questions.explanation: Showery precipitation is characteristic of cumulonimbus clouds due to convective activity.

questions.question: In clouds at temperatures below 0°C an aircraft may encounter icing of the type
questions.explanation: Aircraft icing can be intermediate between rime and clear (glazed) ice depending on droplet size, temperature, and exposure time.

questions.question: The most hazardous cloud for aviation is
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus (CB) clouds are the most hazardous due to turbulence, icing, lightning, hail, and wind shear.

questions.question: Andhi (blinding storms) occur generally over
questions.explanation: Andhi (blinding dust storms) occur generally over North India, particularly during the pre-monsoon season.

questions.question: On approach of a Warm Front temperature
questions.explanation: As a warm front approaches, warm air replaces cold air, causing temperatures to rise.

questions.question: Visibility is poor in a Warm Front
questions.explanation: Poor visibility occurs ahead and during the passage of a warm front due to widespread precipitation and low clouds.

questions.question: A WD with two or more closed isobars, at 2hPa interval, it is termed as
questions.explanation: A Western Disturbance with two or more closed isobars at 2 hPa intervals is classified as a Western Depression.

questions.question: Cyclonic storms are confined almost entirely to the
questions.explanation: Tropical cyclones (cyclonic storms) are confined almost entirely to tropical latitudes, typically between 5° and 20°.

questions.question: Stability of atmosphere is determined by
questions.explanation: Atmospheric stability is determined by comparing the Environmental Lapse Rate (ELR) with the dry and saturated adiabatic lapse rates.

questions.question: Relative humidity depends on
options: A) Moisture content and pressure of the air
B) Temperature of the air only
C) Moisture content and temperature of the air
questions.correctAnswer: C) Moisture content and temperature of the air
questions.explanation: Relative humidity depends on both the actual moisture content and the temperature of the air.

questions.question: Post monsoon
questions.explanation: The post-monsoon season in India occurs during October to December, after the withdrawal of the southwest monsoon.

questions.question: QFE 980, QNH 1000 find elevation:
questions.explanation: Pressure difference of 20 hPa corresponds to approximately 160m elevation (using the standard approximation of 1 hPa ≈ 8m at lower levels).

questions.question: METAR : OVC100 means:
questions.explanation: In METAR, OVC100 means overcast at 100 x 100 ft = 10,000 ft, which is approximately 3000 meters.

questions.question: 18000 feet corresponds to:
questions.explanation: In the standard atmosphere, 18,000 ft (FL180) corresponds approximately to the 500 hPa pressure level.

questions.question: Inversion is an :
questions.explanation: An inversion (temperature increase with height) creates an absolutely stable atmosphere, suppressing vertical motion.

questions.question: Diameter of microburst :
questions.explanation: A microburst is defined as a strong downdraft covering an area less than 4 km in diameter.

questions.question: CI CS AS NS ST in sequence associated with:
questions.explanation: The sequence Cirrus, Cirrostratus, Altostratus, Nimbostratus, Stratus is characteristic of an approaching warm front.

questions.question: Wind speed in a depression:
questions.explanation: In a depression (low pressure system), surface winds are typically 17-27 knots (Beaufort scale 5-6).

questions.question: Relative humidity depends on
questions.explanation: Relative humidity is a function of both the moisture content and the temperature of the air.

questions.question: Rain in coastal areas is more in
questions.explanation: Coastal rainfall is often maximum at night and early morning due to land-sea breeze convergence and nocturnal instability.

questions.question: Fog occurs in cold front
questions.explanation: Fog typically forms ahead of a cold front due to warm, moist air being lifted over advancing cold air.

questions.question: Local Area forecast anyone
questions.explanation: Local Area Forecasts (LAF) typically cover an area within 50 NM of the aerodrome.

questions.question: We are taking off and a large jet took off before us where will the rotation point be
questions.explanation: Wake turbulence vortices sink and move outward; the rotation point for a following aircraft is typically beyond the preceding large jet's rotation point.

questions.question: In moist, unstable air with high surface temperature, which of the following is most likely to occur?
questions.explanation: Moist, unstable air with high surface temperatures favors convective development, producing thunderstorms and towering cumulus.

questions.question: ELR in actual atmosphere:
questions.explanation: The Environmental Lapse Rate (ELR) in the real atmosphere varies with location, season, and weather conditions; it is not constant.

questions.question: Visibility due to fog becomes
options: B) 1000>visibility due to supercooled water droplets and ice crystals
questions.answer: B) 1000>visibility due to supercooled water droplets and ice crystals
questions.explanation: Fog reduces visibility due to suspended supercooled water droplets and ice crystals.

questions.question: What happens to an aircraft encountering a decreasing headwind (headwind windshear)?
options: A) Airspeed increases and aircraft climbs
B) Airspeed decreases and aircraft may sink
C) No effect on aircraft performance
questions.answer: B) Airspeed decreases and aircraft may sink
questions.explanation: Decreasing headwind causes loss of airspeed and lift, potentially making the aircraft sink.

questions.question: In NH winds :
questions.explanation: In the Northern Hemisphere, winds back (change counter-clockwise) and decrease when approaching a low pressure system from the east.

questions.question: Free air temperature, Wet bulb temperature and Dew point temperature are equal when?
questions.explanation: When air is fully saturated (RH = 100%), dry bulb, wet bulb, and dew point temperatures all converge to the same value.

questions.question: 962 on a station model represents?
questions.explanation: The three-digit pressure on a station model (e.g., 962) represents QFF (mean sea-level pressure reduced using actual temperature). The leading 9 or 10 is omitted; 962 = 996.2 or 1096.2 hPa – in this case, 996.2 hPa as QFF.

questions.question: The saturation vapour pressure over water is _____ than over ice.
questions.explanation: Saturation vapour pressure over a water surface is higher than over an ice surface at the same temperature. This difference drives the Bergeron–Findeisen process of ice crystal growth.

questions.question: What kind of barometer is an altimeter?
questions.explanation: An altimeter is an aneroid barometer calibrated to display altitude based on the relationship between atmospheric pressure and height.

questions.question: When heading South in the Southern Hemisphere you experience Starboard drift. What does this indicate?
options: You are flying towards a lower temperature
You are flying away from a lower temperature
You are flying towards a low pressure
You are flying out of a high
questions.correctAnswer: You are flying away from a lower temperature
questions.explanation: In the SH, Buys Ballot's law: stand with wind behind you, low pressure is to your LEFT. With starboard (right) drift heading south, the wind is from the right, meaning you're flying away from the cold/low-temperature region.

questions.question: Glazed (clear) ice is formed by?
questions.explanation: Clear/glaze ice forms when large supercooled water droplets strike the airframe and spread before freezing, forming a clear, dense, hard ice layer.

questions.question: In AC (lenticularis) clouds, which type of icing is seen in mountainous areas?
questions.explanation: Altocumulus lenticularis clouds in mountain wave areas contain supercooled water droplets and can cause severe icing.

questions.question: In the Southern Hemisphere, if you are flying from high to low pressure, winds are coming from?
questions.explanation: In the SH, geostrophic wind blows with low pressure to the LEFT of the wind direction. Flying from H to L in SH, the wind comes from the right.

questions.question: In the Southern Hemisphere, around a low, wind blows?
questions.explanation: In the SH, the Coriolis effect causes winds to deflect to the LEFT, so circulation around a low pressure is CLOCKWISE (opposite to NH).

questions.question: Severe icing in CB is seen between 0°C to −20°C level. Below −20°C, severe icing is?
questions.explanation: Below −20°C, supercooled liquid water droplets are scarce as ice crystals dominate; severe icing becomes not significant.

questions.question: In Jammu & Kashmir and temperate latitudes, more rainfall is seen in?
questions.explanation: J&K and northern temperate latitudes receive precipitation from Western Disturbances during winter months.

questions.question: Corona is associated with which cloud?
questions.explanation: Corona is an optical phenomenon caused by diffraction of light by small water droplets, typically associated with thin altostratus or altocumulus clouds.

questions.question: Stable air is indicated by?
questions.explanation: Stable air produces stratiform clouds and steady, continuous precipitation; unstable air produces convective clouds and showery precipitation.

questions.question: What happens to the aircraft altimeter as an active cold front is passing?
questions.explanation: As a cold front passes, pressure first rises sharply (cold air advancing) and then may settle; some sources indicate pressure drops ahead then rises sharply after. The standard DGCA answer is: increase first then decrease (or rises after passage).

questions.question: TAF validity periods are?
questions.explanation: ICAO TAF validity: short TAF = 9 hours; long TAF = 24 or 30 hours (DGCA India uses 9 hr and 30 hr).

questions.question: Most favourable temperature range for aircraft icing?
questions.explanation: The highest concentration of supercooled water droplets occurs between 0°C and −20°C, making this the most favourable temperature range for icing.

questions.question: Coldest temperature of the day is reached approximately?
questions.explanation: Minimum temperature is reached about 30–60 minutes after sunrise because Earth continues to lose heat by radiation just after sunrise before solar heating reverses the trend.

questions.question: Advection fog forms when?
options: Warm moist air moves over a cold surface
Cold air moves over warm water
questions.correctAnswer: Warm moist air moves over a cold surface
questions.explanation: Advection fog forms when warm, moist air is transported horizontally over a cooler surface, cooling the air to below its dew point.

questions.question: Radiation fog is likely to happen?
questions.explanation: Radiation fog is most dense around or just after sunrise when nocturnal cooling is complete, but it typically disperses within a few hours as solar heating begins.

questions.question: At a warm front, what happens?
questions.explanation: At a warm front, the warm, less dense airmass rises up and over the retreating cold airmass ahead of it.

questions.question: At a warm occlusion, what happens?
questions.explanation: In a warm occlusion, the cold air behind the cold front is colder than the air ahead of the warm front; the warm sector is lifted aloft over the less cold air ahead.

questions.question: A gale is defined as wind speed of?
questions.explanation: By Beaufort scale, a gale (Beaufort Force 8) corresponds to wind speeds of 34–40 knots mean speed.

questions.question: A temperature inversion (absolute stability) represents which lapse rate condition?
questions.explanation: An inversion is a negative Environmental Lapse Rate – temperature increases with altitude. It represents absolutely stable conditions.

questions.question: Flying from Delhi to Kolkata at 10 km in pre-monsoon season, what winds are experienced?
questions.explanation: In pre-monsoon (March–May), the STJ has not yet retreated; at 10 km over India, westerly winds (Sub-Tropical Jet) prevail.

questions.question: Altocumulus lenticular (AC lenticularis) clouds are associated with?
questions.explanation: Altocumulus lenticularis clouds form in the crests of mountain/lee waves and are a reliable indicator of wave activity.

questions.question: No precipitation is seen in which cloud type?
questions.explanation: Cirrus clouds are composed entirely of ice crystals at high altitudes; any precipitation they produce evaporates before reaching the ground (virga) and they don't produce significant precipitation.

questions.question: No icing is seen in which cloud type?
questions.explanation: Cirrocumulus clouds are composed entirely of ice crystals at high altitudes; they do not contain supercooled water droplets and therefore produce negligible icing.

questions.question: Freezing rain occurs when?
options: Supercooled water droplets fall through colder air and freeze to form freezing rain
questions.correctAnswer: Supercooled water droplets fall through colder air and freeze to form freezing rain
questions.explanation: Freezing rain occurs when rain falls from a warm layer aloft through a shallow sub-freezing layer near the surface; droplets remain liquid (supercooled) and freeze on contact with surfaces.

questions.question: Nacreous (Mother of Pearl) clouds are found in which layer?
questions.explanation: Nacreous clouds (polar stratospheric clouds) form in the lower stratosphere at heights of 15–25 km, mainly in polar regions in winter.

questions.question: DALR (Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate) is?
questions.explanation: The DALR is approximately 9.8°C/km or ~3°C/1000 ft (1°C/100 m). This is the rate at which unsaturated air cools when lifted adiabatically.

questions.question: ISA lapse rate per 1000 ft is?
questions.explanation: The ISA (ICAO Standard Atmosphere) lapse rate is 6.5°C/km = approximately 1.98°C/1000 ft in the troposphere.

questions.question: Temperature at FL160 was −22°C; at FL90, what is the OAT (using ISA lapse rate)?
questions.explanation: FL160 to FL90 = 7,000 ft descending. Using ISA LR of 2°C/1000 ft: temp increases by 14°C. −22 + 14 = −8°C.

questions.question: Tropical Revolving Storms (TRS) move faster over which surface?
questions.explanation: TRS accelerate over open ocean where there is no friction from terrain; over land they slow down and weaken due to surface friction and reduced moisture.

questions.question: TRS (Tropical Revolving Storms) occur at which latitude range?
questions.explanation: TRS form between 5° and 20° latitude (where Coriolis force is sufficient for rotation but SST is warm enough ≥26.5°C).

questions.question: On the upper surface of mountain waves, the air is?
questions.explanation: The upper surface of wave clouds and rotors can have locally unstable conditions and turbulence, especially at the crests.

questions.question: Jet stream and CAT can be recognised by?
questions.explanation: Streaks or bands of cirrus cloud aligned with the upper-level wind indicate the presence of jet streams; CAT is associated with jet stream shear zones.

questions.question: Poor visibility is associated with?
questions.explanation: In anticyclones, subsidence inversion traps moisture and pollutants near the surface; calm winds allow fog, haze, and mist to persist, causing poor visibility.

questions.question: Vertical downward movement of air is called?
questions.explanation: Subsidence is the slow, large-scale sinking of air in high pressure systems, associated with stability and clear skies.

questions.question: Outside pressure at 18,000 ft (FL180) is?
questions.explanation: In ISA, the 500 hPa pressure level corresponds to approximately 18,000 ft (5,574 m). This is a standard pressure altitude used in meteorology.

questions.question: The temperature in ISA at 17 km is?
questions.explanation: In ISA, the tropopause is at 11 km with temperature −56.5°C. Above 11 km up to 20 km the temperature remains constant at −56.5°C; at 17 km it is still −56.5°C.

questions.question: A region between two Lows and two Highs is?
questions.explanation: A Col (saddle point) is the neutral area found between two highs and two lows on a pressure chart; it is an area of light winds and poor visibility.

questions.question: Semi-diurnal pressure changes are most pronounced in?
questions.explanation: Semi-diurnal pressure variation (two peaks and two troughs per day) is most pronounced in the tropics due to thermal tidal effects.

questions.question: The instrument for recording pressure is called?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure; a barograph is the recording version. An anemograph records wind speed/direction; a hygrograph records humidity.

questions.question: 850 hPa in ISA corresponds to which level?
questions.explanation: In ISA, the 850 hPa pressure level corresponds to approximately 5,000 ft (1,524 m / ~1,500 m) above MSL.

questions.question: Diurnal variation of temperature is greatest when wind is?
questions.explanation: Calm winds allow maximum nocturnal cooling and maximum daytime heating, resulting in the greatest diurnal temperature range.

questions.question: An air parcel is lifted until it gets saturated. The temperature attained by it is called?
questions.explanation: The wet bulb temperature is the temperature to which air is cooled by evaporation; when an air parcel is lifted adiabatically to saturation (LCL), the temperature attained equals the wet bulb temperature.

questions.question: Warmer the earth, _____ will be the nocturnal radiation?
questions.explanation: Stefan-Boltzmann law: radiated energy is proportional to T⁴. A warmer earth surface radiates more intensely (long-wave radiation) at night.

questions.question: Hot bodies (like the sun) radiate?
questions.explanation: Wien's Law: hotter bodies radiate at shorter wavelengths. The sun (~6000 K) radiates mainly short-wave radiation (UV/visible/near-IR); Earth (~288 K) radiates long-wave (IR).

questions.question: On a rainy day compared to a sunny day, the runway length required is?
questions.explanation: A wet/rainy runway has reduced braking coefficient (lower friction), increasing the landing roll; more runway length is required to stop safely.

questions.question: The spread (difference) between free air temperature and dew point temperature is _____ when air is saturated.
questions.explanation: When air is saturated (RH = 100%), the dry bulb temperature equals the dew point temperature, so the spread is zero (least/minimum).

questions.question: Sea breeze sets in by _____ and dies off at _____?
questions.explanation: Sea breeze begins during the day (typically mid-morning) when land warms faster than the sea, and dies off at night when temperatures equalize.

questions.question: RVR is reported when visibility falls below?
questions.explanation: ICAO Annex 3: RVR is reported when the prevailing visibility is less than 1,500 m or when RVR is less than 1,500 m.

questions.question: Showers occur from?
questions.explanation: Showers (RA SHRA, RASN, GR) are convective precipitation from CB (and to a lesser extent towering Cu). Continuous rain comes from NS/AS.

questions.question: To avoid icing in cloudy conditions, a pilot is advised to fly through a cloud that shows which optical phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Corona indicates small water droplets (less icing hazard). Halo indicates ice crystals (negligible icing). Flying through corona clouds (water droplet clouds) avoids the worst icing. Avoid clouds with halo as they indicate ice-only composition but those have negligible icing; the DGCA standard answer is Corona for 'to avoid icing'.

questions.question: Lenticular clouds indicate the presence of?
questions.explanation: Altocumulus lenticularis form in the wave crests of mountain (lee) waves and are a reliable visual indicator of wave activity.

questions.question: Inversion is a _____ Lapse Rate (LR)?
questions.explanation: An inversion has a negative environmental lapse rate – temperature increases with altitude instead of decreasing.

questions.question: Rainfall in the temperate latitudes is more in?
questions.explanation: Temperate latitudes (30–60°) receive most precipitation in winter due to increased frontal activity from mid-latitude cyclones and Western Disturbances.

questions.question: In CB, icing may range from light to severe up to the −20°C level. Below this temperature, severe icing is?
questions.explanation: Below −20°C, supercooled water drops are scarce as the water is mostly frozen; severe icing decreases and becomes not significant below −20°C.

questions.question: Icing _____ the stalling speed appreciably?
questions.explanation: Ice accretion increases weight, reduces lift (disrupts aerofoil shape), and increases drag, which effectively raises the stalling speed significantly.

questions.question: Norwesters affect?
questions.explanation: Norwesters (Kal Baisakhi) are violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms occurring over northeast India, particularly West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, and Assam.

questions.question: The airmass which originated over a land area in the polar region is?
questions.explanation: Polar Continental (Pc) airmass originates over land at high latitudes; it is cold and dry (low moisture content).

questions.question: If a warm airmass overtakes a cold airmass, it is called?
questions.explanation: A warm front forms when the advancing warm airmass rides over the retreating cold airmass.

questions.question: Line squall occurs about 100–300 km ahead of?
questions.explanation: Squall lines (pre-frontal squalls) form 100–300 km ahead of a cold front due to instability in the warm sector.

questions.question: A Western Disturbance (WD) originates over?
questions.explanation: Western Disturbances are extra-tropical low pressure systems that originate over the Mediterranean, Caspian, and Black Seas and travel eastward, bringing winter precipitation to NW India.

questions.question: The Tropical Jet (TJ) stream over India is?
questions.explanation: The Tropical Easterly Jet (TEJ) flows from east to west over the Indian subcontinent during the SW monsoon, at approximately 150–200 hPa.

questions.question: TRS occurs over Indian seas in?
questions.explanation: Tropical Revolving Storms over the Indian Ocean and Bay of Bengal typically form between 5° and 15° N latitude, where Coriolis force is sufficient for spin-up.

questions.question: The most dangerous part of the cyclone is?
questions.explanation: The eye wall surrounds the calm eye with the most intense convection, highest winds, and heaviest rainfall – the most dangerous part of a tropical cyclone.

questions.question: Pressure gradient over West Coast of India is steep during?
questions.explanation: During the active SW monsoon (Jun–Sep), the steep pressure gradient between the Arabian Sea High and the continental thermal low drives vigorous SW winds over the West Coast.

questions.question: The poleward-moving air that piles up in the subtropical regions forms a high pressure belt called?
questions.explanation: Subtropical highs (Horse Latitudes, ~30° N/S) form where the descending branch of the Hadley cell piles up air, creating persistent high pressure belts.

questions.question: The validity of Landing Forecast (TREND) is?
questions.explanation: TREND (Landing Forecast) appended to METAR is valid for 2 hours from the time of the METAR observation.

questions.question: SPECI is issued when?
questions.explanation: SPECI (Special Observation) is issued when ANY ONE of the specified criteria is met (wind change, visibility, RVR, weather, cloud, temperature thresholds).

questions.question: The temperature at FL110 is −12°C. What will the temperature be at FL140 if ICAO standard lapse rate is applied?
questions.explanation: FL110 to FL140 = 3,000 ft climbing. At ISA LR of 2°C/1000 ft: temperature decreases by 6°C. −12 − 6 = −18°C.

questions.question: The spread (difference) between free air temperature and dew point temperature when air is saturated is?
questions.explanation: At saturation (RH = 100%), dry bulb = dew point, so the spread is zero (minimum/least).

questions.question: The radiation fog forms due to?
options: Heating of the earth during day
Radiational cooling of earth at night
questions.correctAnswer: Radiational cooling of earth at night
questions.explanation: Radiation fog forms when the earth's surface loses heat by long-wave radiation on a clear night, cooling the air above to below dew point.

questions.question: For the formation of radiation fog, which conditions are required?
options: Sufficient moisture, cloudy sky, nil wind
Sufficient moisture, clear sky, light wind
Sufficient moisture, cloudy sky, strong wind
questions.correctAnswer: Sufficient moisture, clear sky, light wind
questions.explanation: Radiation fog requires: adequate moisture (high RH), clear sky (for effective radiative cooling), and light wind (2–7 kt to mix the fog layer without dispersing it).

questions.question: On either side, perpendicular to the _____, pressures rise?
questions.explanation: On either side perpendicular to a TROUGH (an elongated low), pressure rises toward the flanking ridges/highs.

questions.question: Norwesters normally occur during?
questions.explanation: Norwesters (Kal Baisakhi) are convective thunderstorms triggered by maximum daytime heating; they are most frequent in the afternoons over NE India.

questions.question: An altimeter always measures the height of an aircraft above?
options: Datum level at which its sub-scale is set
questions.correctAnswer: Datum level at which its sub-scale is set
questions.explanation: An altimeter measures height above whatever pressure datum is set on the sub-scale (QNH, QFE, QNE/1013). It always reads height above the sub-scale pressure level.

questions.question: Ice pellets on the ground are evidence that?
options: There are thunderstorms in the area
There may be freezing rain at a higher level
questions.correctAnswer: There may be freezing rain at a higher level
questions.explanation: Ice pellets (sleet) form when raindrops fall through a sub-freezing layer and partially freeze; their presence at the surface indicates freezing rain (or rain) exists at a higher, warmer level.

questions.question: What causes wind at low levels?
questions.explanation: Wind is driven by the Pressure Gradient Force (PGF) – air moves from high to low pressure. At low levels, friction modifies the geostrophic balance.

questions.question: On a weather map where isobars are closely packed, the surface winds are likely to be?
options: Strong and blowing across the isobars
questions.correctAnswer: Strong and blowing across the isobars
questions.explanation: Closely packed isobars = steep pressure gradient = strong winds. At the surface, friction causes winds to blow slightly across isobars (at 10–30° toward low pressure).

questions.question: Height of the tropopause?
questions.explanation: Tropopause height decreases from ~16 km at equator to ~8–9 km at poles; it also varies with season, being higher in summer than winter.

questions.question: A moist stable air mass forced to rise against a mountain range – what might you expect?
questions.explanation: Moist stable air flowing over a mountain produces cap clouds (orographic cloud on the windward side) and lee waves/standing waves on the leeward side.

questions.question: SIG Weather Charts are issued _____ times a day?
questions.explanation: ICAO significant weather (SIGWX) charts are issued 4 times per day (at 0000, 0600, 1200, and 1800 UTC) to cover the 24-hour period.

questions.question: Free air temperature, Wet bulb temperature and Dew point temperature are equal when?
questions.explanation: All three temperature measures converge only when air is fully saturated (RH = 100%); at saturation, dry bulb = wet bulb = dew point.

questions.question: What affects how much water vapour the air can hold?
questions.explanation: The capacity of air to hold water vapour (saturation vapour pressure) depends on temperature; warmer air can hold more water vapour.

questions.question: In ISA, the mean sea level temperature is?
questions.explanation: ISA standard sea-level conditions: Temperature = +15°C, Pressure = 1013.25 hPa, Density = 1.225 kg/m³.

questions.question: The temperature at FL110 is −5°C. What will the temperature be at FL050 if the ICAO standard lapse rate is applied?
questions.explanation: FL110 to FL050 = descent 6,000 ft. ISA LR 2°C/1000 ft → +12°C. −5 + 12 = +7°C.

questions.question: The favourable pressure system for formation of fog is?
questions.explanation: Fog forms in anticyclones (highs) and cols (neutral pressure areas) where winds are calm or light, allowing surface cooling and moisture accumulation.

questions.question: Icing _____ the stalling speed appreciably?
questions.explanation: Ice accretion increases aircraft weight and disrupts the aerofoil shape, reducing lift and increasing drag, which raises the stalling speed.

questions.question: Hail is most likely to fall from a cloud?
questions.explanation: Hail forms in Cb clouds with strong updrafts (strong vertical development) that suspend hailstones for repeated cycling through regions of supercooled water and ice.

questions.question: In clouds at temperatures below 0°C, an aircraft may encounter icing of the type?
questions.explanation: In most icing conditions below 0°C, a mixture of rime and clear ice occurs (mixed ice), depending on droplet size, temperature, and airspeed.

questions.question: The descending branch of the Hadley cell, marked by calm winds and high pressure at the surface, is called?
questions.explanation: Horse Latitudes (~30° N/S) mark the subtropical high pressure belts where the descending branch of the Hadley cell creates calm winds and high pressure (also called subtropical highs).

questions.question: To dissipate cloud requires?
questions.explanation: Cloud dissipates when descending air (subsidence) warms adiabatically, increasing the temperature above the dew point and evaporating cloud droplets.

questions.question: The cloud which causes Halo has _____ chances of ice accretion?
questions.explanation: Halo is produced by ice crystals (in Cs or Ci clouds); these clouds have negligible liquid water content, making ice accretion negligible.

questions.question: Break in monsoon occurs when the axis of monsoon trough is along?
questions.explanation: A break in the monsoon occurs when the monsoon trough shifts northward to the foothills of the Himalayas, causing rainfall to cease over most of India.

questions.question: The monsoon current over the West Coast of India is?
questions.explanation: The SW monsoon current over the west coast is a southwesterly flow driven by the cross-equatorial flow from the Arabian Sea High.

questions.question: CAVOK is issued when?
questions.explanation: CAVOK requires ALL THREE conditions simultaneously: visibility ≥ 10 km, no significant weather, and no cloud below 1,500 m or MSA and no Cb.

questions.question: Lenticular clouds indicate the presence of?
questions.explanation: Altocumulus lenticularis form in the crests of mountain/lee waves and reliably indicate wave activity.

questions.question: The conditions necessary for the formation of a thunderstorm are?
options: Steep lapse rate, adequate supply of moisture, and trigger action
questions.correctAnswer: Steep lapse rate, adequate supply of moisture, and trigger action
questions.explanation: Three conditions are necessary: (1) atmospheric instability (steep lapse rate), (2) adequate moisture, and (3) a trigger mechanism (heating, orography, or frontal lifting).

questions.question: 18,000 ft height in ISA corresponds to which pressure level?
questions.explanation: In ISA, 18,000 ft (~5,486 m) corresponds to the 500 hPa level; this is a standard reference level in meteorology.

questions.question: Airframe icing occurs below 0°C. Its probability decreases progressively below −20°C because the proportion of supercooled water drops?
questions.explanation: Below −20°C, ice crystals increasingly dominate over supercooled water droplets; fewer liquid drops means less icing hazard.

questions.question: During the passage of a cold front, winds?
options: Veer and are of moderate strength
questions.explanation: As a cold front passes, the wind suddenly becomes squally (gusty, shifting direction), associated with the Cb activity along the front.

questions.question: In TCU (Towering CU), icing may range from light to severe type at least up to which level?
questions.explanation: In TCU and CB, icing ranges from light to severe up to the −20°C level; below −20°C severe icing is not significant.

questions.question: What is the most common freezing precipitation?
questions.explanation: Freezing rain (FZRA) and freezing drizzle (FZDZ) are the most commonly reported forms of freezing precipitation, associated with temperature inversions and warm fronts.

questions.question: Water vapour is transparent to terrestrial radiation?
questions.explanation: Water vapour is NOT transparent to all terrestrial (long-wave) radiation; it absorbs strongly in certain bands (especially 5–8 µm) but has an 'atmospheric window' (8–12 µm) where it is partially transparent.

questions.question: What is subsidence?
questions.explanation: Subsidence is the slow, large-scale sinking of air associated with anticyclones and ridges, causing adiabatic warming and stability.

questions.question: The life of a Cb cell is usually?
questions.explanation: A single Cb cell completes its life cycle (cumulus, mature, dissipating stages) in approximately 2–3 hours.

questions.question: What clears radiation fog?
questions.explanation: Radiation fog is cleared by: (1) surface heating (solar radiation after sunrise), (2) increase in wind speed (mechanical mixing), or (3) advection of drier air.

questions.question: When the altitude of an aircraft on the ground reads the aerodrome elevation, the altimeter sub-scale is set to?
questions.explanation: QNH causes the altimeter to read elevation above MSL. When on the ground, with QNH set, the altimeter reads the aerodrome elevation.

questions.question: A map with 2 or more closed isobars at 2 hPa interval is termed as?
questions.explanation: A depression (low pressure system) on a synoptic chart is characterised by at least 2–3 closed isobars at 2 or 4 hPa intervals around the centre.

questions.question: During takeoff behind a departing large jet aircraft, the pilot can minimise the hazard of wing-tip vortices by?
options: Rotating before the large aircraft's rotation point and climbing above its flightpath
questions.correctAnswer: Rotating before the large aircraft's rotation point and climbing above its flightpath
questions.explanation: Wingtip vortices sink below the flight path; to avoid them, rotate before the preceding aircraft's rotation point and climb above/upwind of its flightpath.

questions.question: Which of these 2 phenomena form in the transition zone between two airmasses?
questions.explanation: Both fronts (at surface) and jet streams (at upper levels) form along the transition zone (frontal zone) between warm and cold airmasses.

questions.question: For mountain waves to form, the atmosphere should be _____ at higher levels above the ridge?
questions.explanation: A stable layer above the ridge is required to set up the oscillatory wave pattern in the lee of a mountain range.

questions.question: The vertical extent of a fog layer depends primarily on?
questions.explanation: Fog extends up to the base of the temperature inversion above it; the inversion acts as a lid preventing the fog from mixing upward.

questions.question: With all things being equal, in a low having equally-spaced circular isobars, where is the wind the fastest?
questions.explanation: If isobars are equally spaced throughout (uniform pressure gradient), wind speed is the same everywhere in the pattern. The question tests that equal spacing means equal gradient everywhere.

questions.question: Hazardous windshear is commonly encountered near?
questions.explanation: Low-level windshear (LLWS) is most hazardous near thunderstorms (microburst/outflow) and temperature inversions where sharp wind changes occur.

questions.question: Visibility in a warm front sector – when is it poor?
options: Ahead of and during the warm front
questions.correctAnswer: Ahead of and during the warm front
questions.explanation: Extensive cloud and precipitation ahead of a warm front cause poor visibility; it may improve temporarily in the warm sector behind the front.

questions.question: Severe icing is found in which cloud?
questions.explanation: Cb clouds can produce severe icing at 0°C to −20°C level due to very high concentrations of supercooled water droplets and strong updrafts.

questions.question: Minimum temperature is reached at?
questions.explanation: Earth continues to lose heat by radiation just after sunrise; temperature minimum is reached about 30–60 minutes after sunrise.

questions.question: If QFE, QNH, and QFF of an airport have the same value, the airport elevation is at?
questions.explanation: QNH=QFE only when there is no altitude correction (aerodrome at MSL). QFF=QNH at MSL. All three are equal when the aerodrome is at sea level.

questions.question: Precipitation in the form of showers occurs mainly from?
questions.explanation: Showery precipitation is convective, falling from CB and TCU clouds with intermittent intensity and rapid start/stop.

questions.question: Stage of predominant downfall in a thunderstorm?
questions.explanation: The mature stage is the most intense stage of a Cb, characterised by simultaneous updrafts and downdrafts, heavy precipitation, lightning, and hail.

questions.question: The Environmental Lapse Rate (ELR) refers to the rate of change of:
questions.explanation: ELR is the actual decrease in temperature with increasing altitude in the atmosphere.

questions.question: If ELR is greater than DALR, the atmosphere is:
questions.explanation: ELR > DALR means a rising parcel remains warmer than surroundings, leading to instability.

questions.question: The Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate is approximately:
questions.explanation: DALR is about 3°C per 1000 ft (9.8°C per km).

questions.question: A temperature inversion normally indicates:
questions.explanation: Inversion (temperature increasing with height) is a very stable condition.

questions.question: The Coriolis force is zero at the:
questions.explanation: Coriolis force is proportional to sin(latitude), zero at the equator.

questions.question: Geostrophic wind flows:
questions.explanation: Geostrophic wind is in balance between pressure gradient and Coriolis, flowing parallel to isobars.

questions.question: Gradient wind differs from geostrophic wind due to:
questions.explanation: Gradient wind includes centrifugal force due to curved isobars, unlike geostrophic wind.

questions.question: Surface wind differs from geostrophic wind mainly due to:
questions.explanation: Friction near the surface causes wind to cross isobars towards low pressure, reducing speed.

questions.question: A steep pressure gradient results in:
questions.explanation: Steep gradient means closely spaced isobars, producing strong winds.

questions.question: Isobars close together indicate:
questions.explanation: Close isobars imply a steep pressure gradient and strong winds.

questions.question: A cyclone in the Northern Hemisphere has surface winds rotating:
questions.explanation: In NH, cyclones rotate counterclockwise (anticlockwise) and converge inward.

questions.question: An anticyclone is generally associated with:
questions.explanation: Anticyclones have descending, subsiding air, leading to fair weather.

questions.question: The ITCZ is characterized by:
questions.explanation: ITCZ has converging trade winds, rising air, and deep convection.

questions.question: Trade winds blow mainly from:
questions.explanation: Trade winds flow from subtropical highs toward the equatorial low pressure.

questions.question: Jet streams are found near the:
questions.explanation: Jet streams are narrow bands of strong wind near the tropopause level.

questions.question: Core speed of jet streams is highest:
questions.explanation: Polar jet stream is strongest in winter due to increased temperature gradient.

questions.question: Clear Air Turbulence (CAT) is commonly associated with:
questions.explanation: CAT is often found near jet streams due to wind shear.

questions.question: Mountain waves require:
options: Stable air and strong wind perpendicular to ridge
questions.answer: Stable air and strong wind perpendicular to ridge
questions.explanation: Mountain waves need stable air and wind across the ridge >20 kts.

questions.question: Rotor turbulence is most severe:
questions.explanation: Rotor clouds form beneath lenticulars, with severe turbulence.

questions.question: Mechanical turbulence is strongest:
questions.explanation: Rough terrain (mountains, buildings) creates more mechanical turbulence.

questions.question: Radiation fog forms due to:
options: Cooling of air by contact with cold surface
Mixing of warm and cold air
questions.explanation: Radiation fog results from ground cooling by longwave radiation at night.

questions.question: Radiation fog is most likely when winds are:
questions.explanation: Light winds (below 5 kts) allow cooling without mixing, favouring radiation fog.

questions.question: Advection fog forms when:
options: Cold air moves over warm surface
Warm moist air moves over colder surface
questions.answer: Warm moist air moves over colder surface
questions.explanation: Advection fog occurs when warm, moist air passes over a colder surface.

questions.question: Frontal fog is associated mainly with:
questions.explanation: Frontal fog is common ahead of warm fronts due to rain evaporating into cold air.

questions.question: Steam fog forms when:
options: Cold air moves over warm water
Warm air moves over cold land
questions.answer: Cold air moves over warm water
questions.explanation: Steam fog (evaporation fog) forms when cold air passes over warm water, causing evaporation and condensation.

questions.question: The most dangerous cloud for aircraft is:
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus contains severe turbulence, icing, hail, and lightning.

questions.question: Continuous widespread precipitation is usually from:
questions.explanation: Nimbostratus produces steady, widespread rain or snow.

questions.question: Hail formation requires:
questions.explanation: Hail requires strong updrafts to keep ice particles suspended for growth.

questions.question: Supercooled water droplets exist at temperatures:
questions.explanation: Supercooled droplets remain liquid below freezing point (down to -40°C).

questions.question: Structural icing is most likely between:
questions.explanation: Most severe icing occurs in supercooled clouds between 0°C and -20°C.

questions.question: Rime ice is formed by:
questions.explanation: Rime ice forms when small supercooled droplets freeze instantly on impact, trapping air.

questions.question: Clear ice is associated with:
questions.explanation: Clear (glaze) ice forms from large supercooled droplets that freeze slowly, spreading into a smooth layer.

questions.question: Freezing rain occurs when:
options: Warm air aloft, cold surface layer
questions.answer: Warm air aloft, cold surface layer
questions.explanation: Freezing rain requires a warm layer aloft melting snow, then refreezing on sub-zero surface.

questions.question: The tropopause height at the equator is approximately:
questions.explanation: Equatorial tropopause is higher (about 16-18 km) due to strong convection.

questions.question: Temperature in the stratosphere:
questions.explanation: Stratospheric temperature increases due to ozone absorption of UV radiation.

questions.question: Ozone concentration is highest in the:
questions.explanation: The ozone layer is located in the stratosphere, about 15-35 km altitude.

questions.question: Visibility is reduced most by:
questions.explanation: Fog reduces visibility below 1000 m, more severely than rain or haze.

questions.question: Smoke reduces visibility mainly by:
questions.explanation: Smoke particles scatter light, reducing visibility.

questions.question: Diurnal temperature variation is greatest over:
questions.explanation: Deserts have clear skies and dry air, allowing large temperature swings between day and night.

questions.question: What is the ISA temperature at 10,000 ft?
questions.explanation: ISA sea level 15°C, lapse 2°C/1000ft: 15 - (10×2) = -5°C.

questions.question: What is the ISA temperature at 20,000 ft?
Oxygen must be carried by crew when flying above:
questions.explanation: CAR/ICAO require crew to use oxygen above 10,000 ft for flights over 30 minutes, and above 13,000 ft for all crew. For carriage, it is above 10,000 ft.

questions.question: An aircraft is flying at FL100 and the altimeter indicates 10,000 ft. This indicates the air mass temperature is:
questions.explanation: FL100 is pressure altitude 10,000 ft (1013 hPa). If the altimeter reads 10,000 ft when set to 1013, the air mass temperature must be exactly ISA. But options: 'Within ±5°C' is closest because altimeter could be slightly off, but strictly it's ISA. Typically the answer is 'Warmer than ISA'? No, if QNH is standard, altimeter reads pressure altitude. Actually if FL100 and altimeter indicates 10,000 ft, that means the actual pressure altitude is 10,000 ft. Temperature deviation doesn't affect pressure altitude reading; it affects true altitude. This question is tricky. Standard answer: the temperature is ISA. Not an option. Possibly 'Within ±5°C' is acceptable.

questions.question: A surge is defined as a sudden strengthening of wind in the:
options: Both same and different air masses
questions.explanation: A surge is a sudden increase in wind speed within the same air mass, often associated with pressure changes.

questions.question: Nor'westers in India generally originate over the:
questions.explanation: Nor'westers (Kalbaisakhi) originate over the Chota Nagpur Plateau region of eastern India.

questions.question: Synoptic meteorology deals with:
options: Weather systems over large areas using surface and upper-air charts
questions.answer: Weather systems over large areas using surface and upper-air charts
questions.explanation: Synoptic meteorology analyses weather maps and large-scale systems (cyclones, anticyclones, fronts).

questions.question: An aircraft is on the ground and a cold front passes. The altimeter reading will:
questions.explanation: Cold front passage brings colder, denser air; pressure usually rises sharply after the front, so QNH increases, altimeter reading increases.

questions.question: Altostratus is classified as a:
questions.explanation: Altostratus is a medium cloud, base between 6,500 and 20,000 ft.

questions.question: Jet streams are best visualised by observing:
questions.explanation: Jet streams are often marked by bands of cirrus (especially cirrus uncinus).

questions.question: An aircraft flying from Chennai to Kolkata at 14 km altitude during the monsoon season will predominantly encounter:
questions.explanation: At 14 km (about 45,000 ft) during monsoon, the tropical easterly jet stream prevails over India, giving easterly winds.

questions.question: A temperature inversion in the atmosphere indicates:
questions.explanation: Inversion means temperature increases with height, a highly stable condition.

questions.question: In a METAR report, the date and time group represents:
options: UTC date and time of observation
questions.answer: UTC date and time of observation
questions.explanation: METAR time group is in UTC, format DDHHMMZ, e.g., 121530Z.

questions.question: The type of fog most likely experienced by an aircraft in flight is:
questions.explanation: Advection fog can be widespread and persistent, affecting large areas and can be encountered in flight, especially near coastlines.

questions.question: Air temperature is 15°C, dew point is 12°C. The air moves over sea water at 5°C. What type of fog is most likely to form?
questions.explanation: Warm, moist air moving over a colder surface (sea at 5°C) causes advection fog.

questions.question: Two aircraft are on the same altimeter setting. Aircraft A flies in warm air, aircraft B flies in cold air. Which aircraft has the greater true altitude?
options: Both have the same true altitude
questions.explanation: Warm air is less dense; pressure levels are higher. With same altimeter setting, true altitude is higher in warm air (over-read).

questions.question: Wing-tip vortices are caused primarily due to:
options: Spanwise flow from lower to upper wing surface
questions.answer: Spanwise flow from lower to upper wing surface
questions.explanation: Wingtip vortices result from pressure difference causing spanwise flow around the wingtip.

questions.question: The Environmental Lapse Rate (ELR) value is:
questions.explanation: Standard ELR is 6.5°C per kilometre (or approx 2°C per 1000 ft). Option 6.5°C per 1000 m is correct.

questions.question: Nor'westers mainly affect which region of India?
questions.explanation: Nor'westers (Kalbaisakhi) affect West Bengal, Assam, and other eastern/northeastern states, especially in pre-monsoon.

questions.question: Which condition is essential for the formation of a thunderstorm?
options: Stable air and weak lapse rate
questions.explanation: The three ingredients for thunderstorms: moisture, unstable air, and a lifting force.

questions.question: Mountain waves are most likely to form when:
options: Strong wind blows perpendicular to a ridge in stable air
Air is unstable with weak winds
questions.answer: Strong wind blows perpendicular to a ridge in stable air
questions.explanation: Mountain waves require stable air and wind across the ridge at >20 kts.

questions.question: Which optical illusion is considered safe and recommended to fly through?
questions.explanation: Autokinesis is a visual illusion, but no optical illusion is safe. This may be a trick question.

questions.question: In a METAR, the absence of cloud information indicates:
questions.explanation: If no cloud group is present in METAR, it means no clouds are present (SKC or CLR).

questions.question: After the passage of a cold front, surface weather generally becomes:
options: Cold and unstable with good visibility
questions.answer: Cold and unstable with good visibility
questions.explanation: Cold front passage brings cooler, drier air, often with clearing skies, good visibility, but instability may produce showers.

questions.question: The primary reason for icing on aircraft surfaces is:
questions.explanation: Aircraft icing occurs when supercooled liquid water droplets freeze on impact with the airframe.

questions.question: Which process is responsible for cooling of the Earth's surface at night under clear skies?
questions.explanation: The ground cools by emitting longwave radiation (infrared) to space.

questions.question: The Coriolis force is maximum at:
questions.explanation: Coriolis force is proportional to sin(latitude), maximum at poles (90°).

questions.question: Which cloud type is most commonly associated with continuous, widespread precipitation?
questions.explanation: Nimbostratus produces steady, widespread precipitation over a large area.

questions.question: The term lapse rate refers to the rate of change of:
questions.explanation: Lapse rate is the decrease in temperature with increase in altitude.

questions.question: Which front usually produces prolonged poor weather and steady rain?
questions.explanation: Warm fronts bring extensive stratiform clouds and prolonged light to moderate rain.

questions.question: Wind shear is most hazardous during:
questions.explanation: Low-level wind shear near the runway poses the greatest risk due to low altitude and low speed margins.

questions.question: The main source of energy for thunderstorms is:
questions.explanation: Thunderstorms derive energy from the release of latent heat when water vapour condenses.

questions.question: Which cloud type indicates severe turbulence and icing?
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds contain severe turbulence, icing, hail, and lightning.

questions.question: Freezing rain occurs when:
options: Warm air overlies sub-zero surface air
questions.answer: Warm air overlies sub-zero surface air
questions.explanation: Freezing rain requires a warm layer aloft melting snow, then refreezing on sub-zero surface.

questions.question: The pressure gradient force acts from:
questions.explanation: Pressure gradient force is directed from high to low pressure, perpendicular to isobars.

questions.question: Which condition favours the formation of radiation fog?
options: Clear skies, calm winds, moist air
questions.answer: Clear skies, calm winds, moist air
questions.explanation: Radiation fog requires clear skies for radiational cooling, light wind, and high humidity near the surface.

questions.question: The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is characterized by:
questions.explanation: ITCZ is where trade winds converge, causing rising air, cloudiness, and heavy rainfall.

questions.question: Which wind is associated with local heating and cooling between land and sea?
questions.explanation: Sea and land breezes are thermally driven diurnal winds.

questions.question: An increase in dew point temperature indicates:
questions.explanation: Dew point is a direct measure of atmospheric moisture; higher dew point means more water vapour.

questions.question: Which atmospheric condition suppresses vertical cloud development?
questions.explanation: An inversion acts as a cap, preventing vertical convection and cloud growth.

questions.question: The freezing level is defined as the altitude where:
questions.explanation: The freezing level is the altitude at which the temperature is 0°C.

questions.question: Turbulence associated with clear air at high altitude is called:
questions.explanation: CAT occurs in cloud-free skies, typically near jet streams or mountain waves.

questions.question: Which weather phenomenon is most likely to cause microbursts?
questions.explanation: Microbursts are intense downdrafts associated with thunderstorms, especially during the mature stage.

questions.question: In the Southern Hemisphere, a low-pressure system has its centre:
questions.explanation: In the Southern Hemisphere, low-pressure systems are warm-cored (tropical cyclones) or cold-cored (extratropical). However, extratropical lows are cold-cored, but the statement is ambiguous. Typically, tropical lows are warm; extratropical are cold. The question likely refers to cyclonic systems in general, but given options, 'Warmer than surroundings' is correct for tropical cyclones. Surface wind circulation in SH is clockwise, but that is a characteristic, not the centre condition. The centre of a low is usually warmer than surroundings in a tropical system. I'll select 'Warmer than surroundings' as common answer.

questions.question: Which side of a mountain generally experiences worse flying conditions?
questions.explanation: The leeward side (downwind) has turbulence, rotors, and mountain waves, making it more hazardous than the windward side.

questions.question: The geostrophic force balance is most closely achieved:
options: At higher altitudes away from friction
questions.answer: At higher altitudes away from friction
questions.explanation: Geostrophic balance (pressure gradient = Coriolis) is achieved above the friction layer (about 2000-3000 ft AGL).

questions.question: The geostrophic force is least effective:
questions.explanation: Coriolis force is zero at the equator, so geostrophic balance cannot be achieved there.

questions.question: The standard lapse rate in the troposphere is approximately:
questions.answer: 3°C per 1000 ft? Actually 6.5°C per km = about 2°C per 1000 ft. But options: 3°C per 1000 ft is dry adiabatic, not standard. 6.5°C per 1000 m is correct per km, but not per 1000 ft. The standard environmental lapse rate is 1.98°C per 1000 ft ≈ 2°C per 1000 ft. None of these is exactly correct. However, 6.5°C per 1000 m (6.5°C/km) is the standard. So option C: '6.5°C per 1000 m' is correct.
questions.explanation: Standard tropospheric lapse rate is 6.5°C per kilometer (approximately 2°C per 1000 ft). The option '6.5°C per 1000 m' is the closest correct statement.

questions.question: If the environmental lapse rate is less than the standard lapse rate, the atmosphere is considered:
questions.explanation: ELR < standard (or < DALR) indicates a stable atmosphere because rising air cools faster than the environment.

questions.question: Most tropical cyclones affecting India occur during:
questions.explanation: Cyclones in the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea occur mainly in pre-monsoon (April-May) and post-monsoon (October-November) periods.

questions.question: Radiation fog is most likely to form under which conditions?
options: Clear skies, light winds, and moist air
questions.answer: Clear skies, light winds, and moist air
questions.explanation: Radiation fog requires radiational cooling on clear nights, calm or light wind, and sufficient moisture near the ground.

questions.question: Diurnal temperature variation is maximum:
options: Over deserts and dry land areas
questions.answer: Over deserts and dry land areas
questions.explanation: Deserts have low humidity and little cloud cover, allowing large day-night temperature swings.

questions.question: If an anticyclone lies ahead of the aircraft in the Northern Hemisphere, the winds encountered will generally be:
questions.explanation: Anticyclones (high pressure) have descending, diverging air, leading to fair weather.

questions.question: Which cloud type is considered the worst for flying?
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds contain severe turbulence, icing, hail, lightning, and microbursts – the most hazardous for aviation.

questions.question: During a break in the southwest monsoon, the pressure gradient over Bihar is generally:
questions.explanation: During a monsoon break, the monsoon trough moves north, leading to weak pressure gradients and reduced rainfall over Bihar.

questions.question: A cold occlusion occurs when:
options: Colder air undercuts cool air ahead of a warm front
questions.answer: Colder air undercuts cool air ahead of a warm front
questions.explanation: In a cold occlusion, the air behind the cold front is colder than the air ahead of the warm front, so it undercuts the cool air, lifting the warm sector aloft.

questions.question: Altostratus clouds are generally found at heights:
questions.explanation: Altostratus is a medium-level cloud, typically between 6,500 and 20,000 ft.

questions.question: At approximately 2000 ft above ground level, wind speed compared to surface wind is:
options: Slightly higher due to reduced friction
questions.answer: Slightly higher due to reduced friction
questions.explanation: Friction decreases with height, so wind speed increases above the surface. At 2000 ft, wind is typically stronger than at the surface.

questions.question: A temperature inversion in the atmosphere indicates:
questions.explanation: An inversion (temperature increasing with height) is a very stable condition, suppressing vertical motion.

questions.question: At the equator, the troposphere extends approximately up to:
questions.explanation: The equatorial tropopause is higher (about 16-18 km) and colder (around -80°C) than at mid-latitudes.

questions.question: Which condition is essential for the formation of mountain waves?
questions.explanation: Mountain waves require stable air and wind direction within 30° of perpendicular to the ridge, with sufficient speed (usually >20 kts).

questions.question: In a rotor cloud associated with mountain waves, turbulence is most severe:
questions.explanation: Severe turbulence is found in the rotor cloud region, which is below the lenticular clouds and often touches the ground.

questions.question: The most dangerous region of a mature cyclone is the:
questions.explanation: The eyewall contains the strongest winds, heaviest rain, and most severe turbulence.

questions.question: Precipitation is most likely to occur when:
questions.explanation: Precipitation requires air to be saturated and some lifting mechanism (convection, orographic, frontal).

questions.question: Fog is most likely to form after the passage of:
questions.explanation: Warm front passage brings warm, moist air over cooler ground, often causing advection fog and stratus clouds.

questions.question: Radiation fog usually forms most commonly:
questions.explanation: Radiation fog forms overnight as the ground cools, reaching maximum intensity just before or after dawn.

questions.question: During a normal southwest monsoon, the monsoon trough is positioned:
questions.explanation: The monsoon trough during active southwest monsoon lies over the northern plains of India (Ganga plains).

questions.question: Structural icing on aircraft commonly occurs at temperatures between:
questions.explanation: Most icing occurs in supercooled clouds between 0°C and -20°C, with the maximum severity around -5°C to -15°C.

questions.question: ISA temperature at 10,000 ft is approximately:
questions.explanation: ISA at sea level +15°C, lapse 2°C/1000ft; at 10,000 ft: 15 - 20 = -5°C.

questions.question: Relative humidity changes primarily due to:
questions.explanation: Relative humidity depends on temperature and moisture content; temperature change alone (without moisture change) affects RH significantly.

questions.question: Which cloud type indicates strong vertical development?
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds are towering, with strong vertical development, reaching the tropopause.

questions.question: Wind shear is most hazardous during:
questions.explanation: Low-level wind shear near the runway can cause sudden loss or gain of airspeed, critical during takeoff and landing.

questions.question: Which process causes cooling of air without heat exchange?
questions.explanation: Adiabatic process involves no heat exchange; rising air expands and cools adiabatically.

questions.question: The Coriolis force is zero at:
questions.explanation: Coriolis force is zero at the equator because the sine of latitude is zero.

questions.question: Which cloud is most commonly associated with continuous precipitation?
questions.explanation: Nimbostratus produces steady, widespread, continuous rain or snow over a long period.

questions.question: A sudden rise in temperature and fall in pressure indicates passage of a:
questions.explanation: Warm front passage brings warmer air and typically a pressure fall before and then gradual leveling. A sudden rise in temperature and pressure fall is characteristic of a warm front approaching.

questions.question: Freezing rain is most likely when:
options: Warm air lies above sub-zero surface air
Entire air mass is below freezing
questions.answer: Warm air lies above sub-zero surface air
questions.explanation: Freezing rain occurs when snow melts in a warm layer aloft and then refreezes on contact with sub-zero surface.

questions.question: Which weather phenomenon is most associated with wind shift, pressure fall, and gusts?
questions.explanation: Thunderstorms produce gust fronts, sudden wind shifts, pressure rises (not fall) ahead? Actually there's a pressure fall ahead, then sharp rise. Given options, thunderstorm is correct.

questions.question: The tropopause acts as:
options: A lid restricting vertical cloud growth
A zone of intense turbulence only
questions.answer: A lid restricting vertical cloud growth
questions.explanation: The tropopause is a stable layer that acts as a cap, limiting the vertical development of cumulonimbus clouds.

questions.question: METAR se SPECI ko decode - BKN100 means?
questions.explanation: BKN100 in METAR means broken clouds at 100 x 100 = 10,000 ft, which is approximately 3000 meters.

questions.question: Prognostic chart validity
questions.explanation: Prognostic (forecast) weather charts are typically valid for 12 hours.

questions.question: When is temp difference highest bw oat and dew point temp
questions.explanation: The difference between OAT and dew point is highest in dry air because dry air has low moisture content, requiring more cooling to reach saturation.

questions.question: Fog is there when
questions.explanation: Fog is commonly associated with low pressure areas and cols (regions between highs and lows) where winds are light and air is stable.

questions.question: The warm part of polar front is
questions.explanation: The warm sector of a polar front is occupied by tropical air mass, while the cold sector has polar air mass.

questions.question: Stable air is associated with
questions.explanation: Stable air is associated with stratiform clouds, steady precipitation, and restricted visibility due to the layered nature of clouds and precipitation.

questions.question: Max day light change is
questions.explanation: The maximum change in daylight hours occurs between summer solstice (longest day) and winter solstice (shortest day).

questions.question: Given temp +2.5°C will be reported as
questions.explanation: In METAR/TAF coding, temperatures are rounded to whole numbers; +2.5°C rounds to 2.

questions.question: Local Area forecast anyone
questions.explanation: Local Area Forecasts (LAF) typically cover an area within 50 NM of the aerodrome.

questions.question: We are taking off and a large jet took off before us where will the rotation point be
questions.explanation: Wake turbulence vortices sink and move outward; the rotation point for a following aircraft is typically beyond the preceding large jet's rotation point.

questions.question: Reversal of Monsoon in the months of (SW to NE)
options: Sept Oct Nov Dec Jan Feb
questions.answer: Sept Oct Nov Dec Jan Feb
questions.explanation: The Southwest monsoon withdraws and reverses to Northeast monsoon during September to February period.

questions.question: During a passage of cold front winds?
options: Veer and are of moderate strength
questions.explanation: Cold fronts are associated with sudden squally winds due to the steep pressure gradient and convective activity.

questions.question: In mountain waves maximum turbulence?
questions.explanation: Maximum turbulence in mountain waves occurs on the leeward side where the air is unstable and rotors form.

questions.question: Diurnal variation is least when
questions.explanation: Diurnal temperature variation is least when skies are overcast and winds are moderate, preventing radiative cooling/heating.

questions.question: Lenticular clouds indicate
questions.explanation: Lenticular clouds are a classic indicator of mountain wave activity.

questions.question: Cumuliform protuberances indicate?
questions.explanation: Cumuliform protuberances indicate atmospheric instability and convective activity.

questions.question: Ice pellets at 8000 feet what to expect?
questions.explanation: Ice pellets indicate a freezing layer above with warmer air below where ice melts partially before refreezing.

questions.question: Fog is reported when visibility is
questions.explanation: Fog is reported when visibility is reduced to less than 1000 meters.

questions.question: The well developed extra tropical cyclonic storm is composed of two main frontal systems and an occluded front, which varies in extent:
options: A stationary Front followed by a warm front
A low with a warm front radiating out Southwards followed by a cold
A warm front and an occluded front
questions.answer: A low with a warm front radiating out Southwards followed by a cold
questions.explanation: A mature extratropical cyclone has a warm front radiating southward and a cold front following it, with an occluded front developing.

questions.question: Monsoon depression travel faster over
questions.explanation: Monsoon depressions travel faster over sea due to less friction compared to land.

questions.question: Pressure decreases as altitude increases becoz:
questions.explanation: Pressure decreases with altitude because the weight of the air column above decreases.

questions.question: The majority of winds on the west coast of India are :
questions.explanation: The west coast of India experiences Southwest monsoon winds during summer and Northeast monsoon winds during winter.

questions.question: Icing _ stalling speed:
questions.explanation: Ice accumulation increases stalling speed by disrupting airflow and increasing weight.

questions.question: QFE 980, QNH 1000 find elevation:
questions.explanation: Pressure difference of 20 hPa corresponds to approximately 160m elevation (1 hPa ≈ 8m at lower levels).

questions.question: Hoar frost formed when airframe:
questions.explanation: Hoar frost forms when the airframe temperature is below the frost point, causing direct deposition of ice crystals.

questions.question: METAR : OVC100 means:
questions.explanation: In METAR, OVC100 means overcast at 10000 ft (100 x 100 ft), which is approximately 3000m.

questions.question: Diurnal variation of sea :
questions.explanation: Over the sea, diurnal temperature variation is less than 1 degree due to water's high specific heat.

questions.question: Pressure altitude is measured:
questions.explanation: Pressure altitude is the altitude indicated when the altimeter is set to 1013.25 hPa (standard sea level pressure).

questions.question: 18000 feet corresponds to:
questions.explanation: In the standard atmosphere, 18,000 ft (FL180) corresponds approximately to the 500 hPa pressure level.

questions.question: Humidity mixing ratio _ when air is lifted adiabatically
questions.explanation: During adiabatic lifting, the mixing ratio remains constant as no moisture is added or removed.

questions.question: Radiation fog:
questions.explanation: Radiation fog requires radiative cooling of the ground, which is less effective over oceans due to water's thermal properties.

questions.question: Low pressure in Southern Hemisphere wind blows:
questions.explanation: In the Southern Hemisphere, winds around a low pressure system blow clockwise (opposite to Northern Hemisphere).

questions.question: Turbulence is more in and:
questions.explanation: Maximum turbulence in mountain waves occurs below the rotor cloud where air is turbulent and unpredictable.

questions.question: Heavy icing is possible in :
questions.explanation: Heavy icing is most likely in Cumulonimbus (CB) clouds due to high liquid water content and strong updrafts.

questions.question: A cold front would have showers from:
questions.explanation: Cold fronts produce showers from cumulonimbus and towering cumulus clouds due to the steep frontal slope and instability.

questions.question: Inversion is an :
questions.explanation: An inversion (temperature increase with height) represents an absolutely stable atmosphere.

questions.question: Rainfall in the temperate latitudes :
questions.explanation: Temperate latitudes typically receive more rainfall in winter due to frontal activity and cyclonic systems.

questions.question: In clouds at temperatures below 0 degree an aircraft may encounter icing of type :
questions.explanation: Aircraft icing can be intermediate between rime and clear (glazed) ice depending on droplet size and temperature.

questions.question: Diameter of microburst :
questions.explanation: A microburst is defined as a downdraft covering an area less than 4 km in diameter.

questions.question: Over valley and foothills TS generally occur during :
questions.explanation: Thunderstorms over valleys and foothills generally occur in the afternoon due to daytime heating and orographic effects.

questions.question: CI CS AS NS ST in sequence associated with:
questions.explanation: The sequence Cirrus, Cirrostratus, Altostratus, Nimbostratus, Stratus is characteristic of an approaching warm front.

questions.question: For mountain waves to form there should be air below the ridge and less stable above it
questions.explanation: Mountain waves require stable air below the ridge level to allow the wave pattern to establish.

questions.question: Wind speed in a depression:
questions.explanation: In a depression (low pressure system), surface winds are typically 17-27 knots (Beaufort scale 5-6).

questions.question: The most dangerous part of the TS
questions.explanation: The eye wall of a thunderstorm contains the strongest updrafts, heaviest precipitation, and most severe turbulence.

questions.question: A monsoon depression slopes with height
questions.explanation: Monsoon depressions in India slope southwestward with height due to the vertical wind shear.

questions.question: During summer season
options: WDs cause TS/DS over Punjab and Rajasthan
Track of WD is southern most
questions.answer: WDs cause TS/DS over Punjab and Rajasthan
questions.explanation: Western Disturbances during summer cause thunderstorms and dust storms over Punjab and Rajasthan.

questions.question: An aircraft flying in winter delhi to kolkata at 6km experiences:
questions.explanation: In winter, Delhi to Kolkata at 6km encounters westerly winds, causing starboard (right) drift in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.question: A part of the sinking air over the subtropical highs flows towards the equator turning west due to coriolis force this surface air is called :
questions.explanation: Trade winds are the surface winds flowing from subtropical highs toward the equator, deflected west by Coriolis force.

questions.question: The descending branch of hadley cells marked by calm winds and high pressure at the surface are called:
questions.explanation: Horse latitudes are the subtropical regions where Hadley cell air descends, creating high pressure and calm winds.

questions.question: Landing forecast is appended to:
questions.explanation: Landing forecasts (TREND) are appended to METAR and SPECI reports.

questions.question: Fog occurs in cold front
questions.explanation: Fog typically forms ahead of a cold front due to the warm, moist air being lifted over the advancing cold air mass.

questions.question: Aerodrome warning for light aircrafts when wind is
questions.explanation: Aerodrome warnings for light aircraft are typically issued when surface winds reach 17 knots or more.

questions.question: Formation of predominant stratiform cloud as context to predominant cumulus cloud dependent on?
questions.explanation: Stratiform clouds form in stable air where lifted air settles in horizontal layers, while cumulus clouds form in unstable air.

questions.question: Stability of air will increase if
questions.explanation: Cooling air from below increases stability by reducing the temperature lapse rate and suppressing vertical motion.

questions.question: Aircraft altimeter showing constant altitude while it is moving toward low pressure zone, then true altitude will be (vise e versa) indicated altitude
questions.explanation: When flying toward a low pressure area with constant indicated altitude, the true altitude decreases because the pressure surface drops.

questions.question: More rains happens in india when
options: Axis of monsoon trough is over gangetic plains
Axis of MT is over NE region
questions.answer: Axis of monsoon trough is over gangetic plains
questions.explanation: Maximum rainfall occurs when the monsoon trough lies over the Gangetic plains, creating strong convergence.

questions.question: At FL140 temp is -12°C so at FL110 will be according to ICAO standard atmosphere
questions.explanation: ISA lapse rate is 2°C per 1000 ft. FL140 to FL110 is 3000 ft difference, so -12 + 6 = -6°C.

questions.question: Hails can be found on which type cloud
questions.explanation: Hail forms in cumulonimbus clouds which have strong updrafts and large vertical development.

questions.question: Fog that freezes on aircraft parked on ground
questions.explanation: Hoar frost forms on parked aircraft when water vapor deposits directly as ice crystals on cold surfaces below freezing.

questions.question: Forms over a/c when aircraft is passing through atmosphere with no clouds but moisture in air at temp below 0°C
questions.explanation: Hoar frost can form in clear air with moisture when the airframe temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: Rain in coastal areas is more in
questions.explanation: Coastal rainfall is often maximum at night and early morning due to land-sea breeze convergence and nocturnal instability.

questions.question: In mountain waves there is air upto ridge
questions.explanation: For mountain wave formation, the air below the ridge level must be stable to allow the wave pattern to develop.

questions.question: In mountain waves there is air above ridge
questions.explanation: Above the ridge, less stable or unstable air allows the wave to break and create turbulence.

questions.question: Pressure is measure with
questions.explanation: A barometer is the instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: Sea breeze sets in _ and dies off at
questions.explanation: Sea breeze sets in during the day and dies off at night when the land cools.

questions.question: If pressure altitude is FL120 and true altitude is 12000ft and QNH is 1013 hPa then in atmosphere
options: Actual temperature is warmer than ISA
Average temperature is equal to ISA temperature at that level
